items.title: Slop in clinical notes
items.body: The edition defines slop as skipped thinking whose cost lands on the reader. In general practice the reader is the next clinician, so a long, generic, unread scribe note is a patient-safety issue. Reading and editing every AI-drafted note before filing, and keeping notes short and specific, applies directly.

items.title: Automation complacency
items.body: The cited finding that more trust in AI goes with less critical checking is a known risk for scribe users. A practical safeguard is deciding in advance what you always verify: medication, doses, allergies, safety-netting and any examination findings the tool could not have heard.

items.title: Disclosure and detection
items.body: Labelling AI-assisted work is sensible for letters and reports as well as notes, including medical examiner and referral documents. Detectors are unreliable, so the control is a named human who can defend every sentence, not software. No Zitron counterpoint was published on this topic.
